intent: Change one thing: the sensor footprint from 16 mm to 12 mm, keeping the ±0.03 m row at 0.015 m spacing, y = 0.04, and the Integrator's kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 controller. The hypothesis is that 16 mm edge noise is raising s-bend steering oscillation. I expect steering_oscillation on the s-bend to fall below 0.168, with progress held near 0.21 and max error still at about 0.062. I do not expect a new best score, and I expect coverage reach to fall to about 0.0485 m. If the score drops below 69.46, I will return to 16 mm in the next iteration, because the footprint is then not the limit. Slalom oscillation should stay below 0.15, so no forward offset.
learning: Expected outcomes: (1) if s-bend oscillation falls and progress holds, footprint noise was a contributor and 12 mm is a candidate for the final design; (2) if line loss rises or progress falls, the 16 mm reach is needed and the 0.0505 m coverage edge is the limit. Please report, in integration feedback, the progress at the first line-loss event on each track, the max error at that moment, and whether the loss occurs at start-up. Also please say whether the controller needs any gain change for the smaller footprint, since the signal scale may change.
rationale: Evidence across iterations 0 to 9 is consistent. The ±0.03 m row at 16 mm with y = 0.04 is the best-raced geometry: 69.46 in iterations 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9, identical each time, so the simulator is deterministic for this layout. Every race ends off track at max error about 0.062 m, against the 0.06 m limit. Body width cannot relax that limit inside its allowed range, and line loss stays at 1.0 to 1.1 events per run. The ±0.04 m row was tested at kp 1.2 in iteration 8 and scored 61.35, so widening is worse on its own, not only at kp 1.0. The open question the Integrator raised is whether 16 mm footprint edge noise adds s-bend steering oscillation (0.168 at iteration 3). I am taking the Integrator's conditional advice: their feedback says to test a 12 mm footprint at the same ±0.03 m spacing if s-bend oscillation stays high. It does, so I am making that change now. The trade-off is reach: a 12 mm footprint at x = ±0.03 covers offsets only to about 0.0485 m, against about 0.0505 m for 16 mm, so I expect some loss of warning before the limit. I am not moving the row forward, because slalom oscillation has stayed at 0.145 to 0.147, below the 0.15 trigger. I am keeping wheels, body and mass fixed. I am not repeating the known 16 mm best this iteration, because I have two iterations left and need evidence on whether the footprint is the cause before I commit the final design. If the 12 mm row does not beat 69.46, the next iteration returns to 16 mm, which is the known floor.
